**Summary:**

The internet originated in the 1960s through ARPANET, a U.S. Department of Defense project, with the first message sent in 1969; the 1983 transition to TCP/IP protocols and Tim Berners-Lee's 1989 invention of the World Wide Web established the modern internet's foundation. The 1993 release of the Mosaic browser democratized web access, leading to the dot-com boom of the late 1990s, which crashed in 2001 but produced enduring giants like Amazon and Google. The mid-2000s saw social media transform communication, while mobile internet after the 2007 iPhone launch and AWS's 2006 cloud computing emergence made the web ubiquitous. Today, over 5 billion people are connected, and the internet underpins virtually all aspects of modern life.
